intent: Ensure every existing Android Viewer shell revalidates the hosted Viewer UI when the app launches.

requestReview.reason: The `/viewer` navigation response changes from a one-hour freshness lifetime to mandatory launch-time revalidation. No timer, Firestore operation, listener, retry, or persistence write is added.
requestReview.assumptions: One Android Viewer shell makes one Firebase Hosting navigation request each time it launches. This request may return the document or a conditional response; it creates zero Firestore document reads and zero writes. Session, device-list, reconnect, WebRTC, and TURN traffic are unchanged.

checks.idle: The Hosting header contains no timer or client loop; after the launch navigation it generates zero idle Firestore reads and writes over 24 hours.
checks.rerender: A server response header cannot add a React render request; rerenders retain the existing Viewer request owners.
checks.concurrency: Each app launch performs its own bounded navigation revalidation without shared mutable request state.
checks.failure: The existing Android WebView error screen remains the network-failure boundary; the cache policy adds no retry loop.
checks.cleanup: No timer, listener, or callback is created, so app shutdown has no new lifecycle owner to clean up.

rollback: Revert the `/viewer` Hosting header commit and redeploy Firebase Hosting; Android APK binaries and registered data remain unchanged.

outcomes.acceptance: Launching an already installed Android Viewer revalidates `/viewer` with Firebase Hosting and receives the currently deployed shared UI instead of treating the prior document as fresh for one hour.
outcomes.physicalGap: A physical relaunch of an already installed Android Viewer remains required after live header verification. Native APK replacement still requires Android installation approval or managed-device privileges.
